question: One of these libraries lets a grouping construct that has no representation of its own stand in for a real container in the host environment, and the shim that makes that work implements the parts of the host contract its author remembered. Three of the operations a real container must support are wrong in the same way: registering interest in an event and then withdrawing it loses track of what was registered, so the withdrawal silently does nothing; dispatching an event through the stand-in behaves differently depending on what kind of real container it is standing inside; and asking where the stand-in sits relative to another element gives an answer that contradicts the tree for the two edge cases - the outermost element of the document, and a stand-in that currently contains nothing at all. Each of these is invisible in the common case and only shows up when the construct is used where a real container would have been. The contract is that a stand-in for a host object must satisfy the host's own contract at its edges, not merely in the middle, and that the tree-shaped questions must be answered from the tree the framework maintains rather than from whatever the host happens to return. Elsewhere in the folder the same problem is handled by refusing to stand in at all: two libraries attach their listeners to a real element they own and route everything through it, so no host contract is ever emulated. Which files emulate a host container incompletely, and which own the delegate-to-a-real-element contract they can be compared against?

anchor.pr_title: [DOM] Fix Fragment removeEventListener dropping tracked listeners

grader_notes.why_cross_repo: ANCHOR: three separate post-pin React PRs all land in ReactFiberConfigDOM.js and all are 100% live at the pin - #37160 'Fragment removeEventListener dropping tracked listeners' (3cba19c97725, 12/12), #37165 'Fragment dispatchEvent when the container is a Document' (305feb9058f3, 1/1) and #37163 'Fragment compareDocumentPosition for documentElement and empty portals' (809280d595b5, 2/2, plus additions to ReactFiberTreeReflection.js, the module that answers tree-shaped questions from the fiber tree). Citations: tldraw and xyflow both decline to emulate a host container - tldraw attaches document- and canvas-level listeners to real elements it owns (useDocumentEvents.ts, useCanvasEvents.ts) and xyflow routes all pointer traffic through its own renderer element (FlowRenderer/index.tsx).
grader_notes.verification_method: (1) All three anchors mined from `pin..origin/main`, pin-is-ancestor True, removed-line liveness 12/12, 1/1 and 2/2 at the pin. (2) Citation paths confirmed with `git cat-file -e <pin>:<path>`. (3) Overlap check: 0 shared (repo,file) pairs - xyflow's prior gold includes container/Pane/index.tsx but not FlowRenderer. (4) Contract check: no v5 or v6 case is about emulating a host object's contract.
grader_notes.difficulty_design: The whole anchor is one very large file, so recall depends on finding the second react file and the three outside citations, none of which shares vocabulary with 'Fragment'. 5 files / 3 repos.
